display.purpose: The author's name on the homepage hero. Used once across the whole site.

headline.purpose: Page h1 and the contact call to action.

title.purpose: Card titles: roles, certifications, tools, articles.

body.purpose: All prose. Capped at 62ch in the hero.

label.purpose: Section labels. Uppercase with .04em tracking on tool pages; PS>-prefixed on the homepage.

mono.purpose: Terminal chrome, shell prompts, exam codes, IP ranges. Anything a machine produced or must consume.

code.purpose: Calculator and policy result values. Uses the Cascadia Code stack rather than the shell mono stack.

shadows.name: hairline-lift
shadows.purpose: The default .glass card. Reads as a crisper border, not as height.

shadows.name: floating-panel
shadows.purpose: Only for elements that overlay content: mobile nav, back-to-top. Dark theme uses rgba(0,0,0,0.45).

shadows.name: backplate-ring
shadows.purpose: White backplates behind third-party logos, which need a light field in both themes.

motion.name: state-standard
motion.purpose: Default for card lift, button hover, border colour changes.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Homepage scroll-reveal of sections. Forced visible under prefers-reduced-motion and inside <noscript>.

motion.name: aurora-drift
motion.purpose: Background atmosphere only. Fully stopped under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single highest-intent action on a page. One per view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: .625rem 1.25rem; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: #0b6fb8; color: #fff; font-family: "Segoe UI", Aptos, Calibri, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: .88rem; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .2s, background .2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #075b98; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #0b6fb8; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action. Borders and fills with the accent on hover rather than carrying it at rest.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: .625rem 1.25rem; border: 1px solid #89afd0; border-radius: 6px; background: #fff; color: #17324d; font-family: "Segoe UI", Aptos, Calibri, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: .88rem; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .2s, border-color .2s, background .2s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #0b6fb8; background: rgba(11,111,184,.09); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #0b6fb8; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Glass Card
components.description: The most-used container on the site. Flat at rest, lifts and borders in accent on hover.
components.css: .ds-card { padding: 22px 26px; border: 1px solid #d8e8f5; border-radius: 8px; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 0 2px #d8e8f5, 0 1px 2px #d8e8f5; font-family: "Segoe UI", Aptos, Calibri, -apple-system, sans-serif; transition: transform .2s, border-color .2s; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: #0b6fb8; } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 4px; font-size: 1.05rem; font-weight: 650; color: #17324d; line-height: 1.3; } .ds-card p { margin: 0; font-size: .78rem; color: #536f88; }

components.name: Filter Input
components.description: The search field that opens nearly every tool page's filter bar.
components.css: .ds-input { min-height: 2.9rem; padding: 0 .85rem; border: 1px solid #89afd0; border-radius: 8px; background: #fff; color: #17324d; font-family: "Segoe UI", Aptos, Calibri, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #536f88; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #0b6fb8; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: View Toggle
components.description: The Cards/List (and sometimes Map) switch shared by nine tool pages. Active segment carries the accent wash.
components.css: .ds-toggle { display: inline-flex; gap: .25rem; padding: .25rem; border: 1px solid #d8e8f5; border-radius: 10px; background: #fff; } .ds-toggle-btn { padding: .45rem .9rem; border: 0; border-radius: 7px; background: transparent; color: #536f88; font-family: "Segoe UI", Aptos, Calibri, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: .85rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background .2s, color .2s; } .ds-toggle-btn:hover { color: #17324d; background: #eef7ff; } .ds-toggle-btn.is-active { background: rgba(11,111,184,.09); color: #0b6fb8; font-weight: 600; } .ds-toggle-btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #0b6fb8; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Client Pill
components.description: A named organisation with its favicon. Fully rounded, lifts on hover.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; padding: 4px 11px 4px 5px; border: 1px solid #d8e8f5; border-radius: 999px; background: #eef7ff; color: #17324d; font-family: "Segoe UI", Aptos, Calibri, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: .76rem; transition: transform .15s, border-color .15s; } .ds-pill:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); border-color: #0b6fb8; } .ds-pill-mark { width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 5px; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #d8e8f5; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Machine state on a data row: availability, taggability, feed health. The only place colour is allowed to shout.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; padding: 2px 9px; border-radius: 999px; font-family: "Segoe UI", Aptos, Calibri, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: .72rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-badge.is-pass { background: #eefaf5; color: #157f57; } .ds-badge.is-fail { background: #fdf2f2; color: #c93636; }

narrative.overview:
This is the workbench of a working Azure engineer that happens to also be his portfolio. The person using it is mid-task: an incident is open, a policy alias needs resolving, a region's zone support has to be confirmed now. Every visual decision answers to that scene. The palette is cool and low-drama so that a green PASS or a red FAIL is the only thing that shouts. Density is deliberately high — a console that makes you scroll to find one value has failed. Type is the OS UI stack, not a personality font, because this should feel like a tool you already know how to operate rather than a designed artifact you have to learn.

The frame around that instrument is a light PowerShell metaphor: a terminal chrome bar on the homepage hero, PS> prefixes on section labels, .\Start-Collaboration.ps1 as a contact heading. It is a costume, worn lightly and only where the site talks about its author. It never enters a tool page, where the data is the point.

The system's real signature is the shared shell: an identical sticky header, aurora backdrop, dismissible banner, footer, theme toggle, and back-to-top across 63 pages built by hand with no build step and no dependencies. Twenty-six unrelated utilities read as one product because that shell never varies. That consistency is not decoration — it is the load-bearing structure of the whole design.
keyCharacteristics: Cool blue-frost neutrals; colour reserved almost entirely for status
Dense, scannable, built for a visitor who arrived from search and needs one answer
Full light/dark parity, both themes measured at WCAG AA
Flat surfaces with hairline borders; elevation is rare and functional
OS-native type stack, monospace only where the terminal metaphor speaks
Zero dependencies, zero build, one shell across every page

rules.name: The Status-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, red and ochre exist to report machine state, never to decorate. If a colour on this site is not answering a question the visitor asked about their data, it should be a neutral.

rules.name: The Two-Palette Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are two independently tuned palettes that share token names, not token values. --cp-warning is #96610a in light and #e4a940 in dark because each was set against its own background. Never resynchronise them.

rules.name: The Composite-Before-You-Judge Rule
rules.body: --cp-accent-soft is an alpha tint and the banner background is a gradient. Both read as transparent from getComputedStyle().backgroundColor. Any contrast check that does not composite the full background stack will report spectacular false failures on this site.

rules.name: The No-Webfont Rule
rules.body: The system font stack is a hard constraint, not a placeholder. A webfont would add a network dependency, a FOUT, and a licence to a site whose entire premise is that it has none.

rules.name: The Machine-Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks text that came from a machine or addresses one. Prose never uses it, and a value the user must copy always does.

rules.name: The Reserve-The-List Rule
rules.body: Every list on this site is rendered from JSON after load. A container that starts at zero height throws the footer up the page and then shoves it back down, which is the single largest source of layout shift here. Any async-filled container gets a min-height (70vh is the house value) so the first paint already occupies the space the data will need.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Intent Rule
rules.body: Cards do not sit raised; they rise translateY(-4px) and switch their border to the accent on hover. Elevation is feedback, never decoration.

rules.name: The Documented-Literal Rule
rules.body: A handful of values are deliberately literal rather than tokenised: the three aurora gradient stops, the three terminal chrome dots, the print neutrals and the white logo backplate. They are recorded in DESIGN.md so they read as system, not drift. Anything else literal is drift.

dos: Do build a new page by copying the most recently built similar page. The shell is the design system; re-typing it from memory is how drift starts.
Do ship every colour in both themes, tuned independently against its own background, and verify both at WCAG AA.
Do reserve height (min-height: 70vh) on any container filled from JSON after load.
Do offset anything sticky from --header-h, never from a hard-coded pixel value.
Do wrap grid floors in min(<floor>, 100%) so they can collapse on a 360px viewport.
Do keep colour for machine status. A neutral is the correct answer for almost everything else.
Do give focus a visible 3px accent outline on :focus-visible.
donts: Don't break light/dark parity. Every new token needs both values, measured — a dark theme that is a washed-out grey inversion of the light one is a regression, not a shortcut.

Don't introduce a build step, a framework, a webfont, or an npm dependency. Each page is one self-contained HTML file with inline <style> and <script>, and that portability is the point. (Leaflet on /azure-regions/ is the single deliberate exception.)
Don't let one page's shell diverge from the other 62. A change to the header, footer, banner or theme toggle is a sitewide codemod plus a pageShell() edit plus a rebuild — or it is not done.
Don't animate layout properties. width, height, padding and margin transitions cause reflow; use transform and opacity.
Don't add a second accent. The site has one interactive colour, and cyan and violet exist only inside a single decorative gradient.
Don't trust a contrast reading without compositing alpha tints and gradient backgrounds first.
